problem: VLN agents generalize poorly to unseen houses. Prior pretraining either used speaker-augmented paths from only the 61 R2R training houses, which have little visual diversity, or used out-of-domain web image-caption data (VLN-BERT on Conceptual Captions), which gives only small gains. Their proxy tasks (masking, pairing, one-step action prediction) also do not teach the temporal alignment between a path and an instruction.
motivation: Navigation instructions are rare on the web. Photos and captions of home interiors, however, are abundant on rental marketplaces like Airbnb, covering hundreds of thousands of visually diverse houses. Existing pretrained models are brittle: they are confused when noun phrases in an instruction are swapped or replaced, which suggests weak temporal and grounding reasoning.
key_idea: Collect a large in-domain dataset from Airbnb listings (BnB: 1.4M indoor images, 0.7M captions), turn its image-caption pairs into VLN-like path-instruction pairs, and pretrain a ViLBERT-style model (Airbert) with masking plus a new shuffling contrastive loss that enforces temporal path-instruction alignment.
insight:
In-domain data matters more than generic web data, and closing the format gap to VLN matters too:
- BnB pretraining without ConCaps already beats VLN-BERT (60.54 vs 59.26 val-unseen SR); stacking ConCaps→BnB-PI reaches 66.52 (Table 2).
- Among the PI-creation strategies, inserting captionless images helps most on its own (66.05 vs 62.71 for naive concatenation). It mimics R2R paths, where many viewpoints are never described (Table 3).
- The shuffling loss adds +2.3 SR when used in pretraining and +3.1 when combined with Speaker data (65.52→68.67, Table 4).
- As an extra fine-tuning negative, shuffling beats hard negatives or keyword highlighting without needing external parsers (Table 5).
- Error analysis shows gains of more than 8 points on noun replace/swap corruptions. Left/right direction discrimination stays near 50% accuracy.
- In few-shot, one training house gives 50.00 vs 22.43 SR for VLN-BERT, showing that in-domain pretraining can substitute for downstream data.
method: BnB dataset: about 150K US Airbnb listings are scraped. Outdoor images are removed with a Places365 ResNet, and invalid or duplicate captions are dropped. The result is 713K image-caption pairs plus 676K captionless images (95/5 train/val split).

PI-pair creation (on the fly): K~U[4,7] image-caption pairs from one listing are concatenated with random connectors ('and', 'then', '.', nothing). Instruction rephrasing fills 11,626 R2R-derived templates (2-7 blanks) with noun phrases from BnB captions, preferring Visual Genome objects. Image merging groups same-room-category images (Places365 labels) to approximate panoramic context. Captionless image insertion adds images with empty captions (N~U[2,K] captioned, the rest captionless). A ViLBERT-based instruction generator fine-tuned on R2R was also tried.

Airbert architecture: a ViLBERT-like two-stream transformer with co-attention. Visual input is Bottom-Up Top-Down region features plus a 5-d location MLP plus an image-order embedding, with [IMG] tokens separating the locations. Text input is the concatenated instruction tokens.

Shuffling loss: for each aligned PI pair, 9 negatives are made by shuffling the image sequence or the caption sequence so that the order no longer matches. The loss is softmax cross-entropy over the alignment logits, used alongside masked language/region modeling.
Staged training: ViLBERT on ConCaps (masking+pairing) → BnB-PI (masking+shuffling) → R2R PI pairs (masking+shuffling, optionally Speaker 178K pairs) → task fine-tuning.

Discriminative adaptation (R2R path selection, as in VLN-BERT): a positive candidate (within 3m of the goal) is ranked against 3 beam-search negatives from EnvDrop plus 2 shuffled-path negatives. At test time the model reranks 30 beam candidates, optionally ensembled with the EnvDrop speaker and follower via a grid-searched linear combination.

Generative adaptation: Airbert serves as the backbone of Recurrent VLN-BERT. The language stream encodes the instruction and its [CLS] becomes the recurrent state; the visual stream updates the state and scores navigable views or objects. Training uses IL + A2C with PREVALENT augmented data for R2R, and scene + object features for REVERIE.

setting.backbone: Airbert: ViLBERT-architecture two-stream transformer (initialized from ViLBERT/ConCaps, pretrained on BnB), fine-tuned; used as path-selection scorer or as Recurrent VLN-BERT backbone
setting.training_data: Conceptual Captions (3.3M IC pairs, via ViLBERT init) + BnB (713K image-caption pairs + 676K captionless images from ~150K Airbnb listings, PI pairs generated on the fly) + R2R train PI pairs + EnvDrop Speaker augmented data (178K PI pairs) for discriminative model; PREVALENT augmented pairs for generative R2R; REVERIE train for REVERIE
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (Faster R-CNN / Bottom-Up Top-Down region features per viewpoint for the discriminative model; ResNet-152 Places365 view features, plus BUTD object features for REVERIE, in the generative model)
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (discriminative: select one of 30 beam-search candidate full paths; generative: select next navigable viewpoint / object)
setting.privileged: Discriminative R2R results use the pre-explored setting: beam search yields 30 candidate trajectories from EnvDrop, which are reranked. Generative (Recurrent VLN-BERT) R2R/REVERIE results use no privileged info.

numbers_note:
- SPL on R2R discriminative tables is printed as a fraction (e.g. 0.63) and converted here to 0-100; path length (PL) is mapped to TL.
- The few-shot tables are inconsistent. For 1 house, main Table 8 gives Airbert val-unseen SR 50.00 (seen 47.88), while appendix Table 11 prints 54.48 unseen. For 6 houses, main gives seen 54.48, appendix prints 50.00 seen. The values 50.00 and 54.48 appear swapped in the appendix. The main-text claim '+27.6% with 1 house' is consistent with 50.00.
- Only 6-house few-shot SR was recorded here. One-shot (1 house) val-unseen SR = 50.00 was omitted.
- A footnote mentions a leaderboard ensemble of Airbert + VLN-BERT + speaker + follower at 78% test-unseen SR, without a full metrics table.
- The R2R ablation tables (Tables 2-5) report SR only.
results:
- Discriminative R2R (reranking 30 beam candidates): single Airbert reaches 68.67 val-unseen SR vs 59.26 for VLN-BERT (+9.4). Ensembled with speaker and follower it reaches 75.01 val-unseen and 77 SR on the R2R test leaderboard (first at submission), vs 73 for VLN-BERT.
- REVERIE: Airbert as the Recurrent VLN-BERT backbone reaches test SR 30.28 / RGS 16.83 / RGSPL 13.28, vs 24.62 / 12.65 / 10.00 for Rec (OSCAR).
- Generative R2R: Rec (Airbert) reaches 62 SR test, on par with Rec (PREVALENT) at 63.
- Few-shot: Airbert trained on only 6 houses (57.97 val-unseen SR) nearly matches VLN-BERT trained on all 61 (59.26).
limitations: The headline R2R SOTA relies on the discriminative path-selection setting. It needs pre-exploration and beam search over 30 candidates plus a speaker/follower ensemble, which makes SPL about 0.01 on the leaderboard and makes it not comparable with single-run agents.
Directional reasoning stays weak: accuracy on left/right-swapped instructions is only about 47-50%. Failure cases involve 'between' and 'on the left'.
In the generative setting on R2R, Airbert only matches the PREVALENT initialization rather than beating it. The instruction-generation strategy is limited by the R2R vocabulary.
